summary: Build shared services capability through operating-model design, service catalogues, KPIs, governance, and transition planning. Enquire about training.
lede: A shared services model brings selected back-office processes together with clear ownership and defined service boundaries. This course is for operations leaders, shared services managers, and finance leaders who need to assess which processes fit, define service catalogue entries, and set performance measures. Participants also practice mapping responsibilities and planning transition controls for finance, HR, procurement, or administration services.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for shared services design, back-office operating models, service performance, or cross-functional transformation. It suits experienced practitioners and leaders who can bring a live or representative finance, HR, procurement, or administration process into the exercises.
modules: Shared Services Strategy and Executive Reporting
prerequisites: You should bring a representative back-office process, existing service measures, or a current transformation challenge where possible. No programming is required. Exercises use provided templates and representative datasets, with Excel-based analysis and dashboard design rather than production-system configuration. Advanced digital workflow and AI-assisted automation topics receive operational application treatment, while enterprise platform deployment remains outside the course scope.
